first.title: Every figure in a report is checked against its source on the day it is sent
first.when: sending a report that holds figures
first.why: a stale figure went out in the January report
first.context: Reports are drafted over several days.
first.false-if: the source is frozen before drafting starts

second.title: A letter to a client is signed by the owner, never by the office
second.when: writing or sending a letter to a client
second.why: two clients asked who had written to them
second.context: Clients know the owner by name.
second.false-if: letters are sent by a named account manager

notes.title: The March figure came from two sheets that disagree
notes.body: The sales sheet and the ledger give different totals for March.

notes.title: The owner had the letter signed in their own name
notes.body: The draft was signed for the office; the owner asked for their own name.

notes.title: The owner again changed the signature to their own name
notes.body: A second letter drafted for the office was re-signed by the owner.
